title: Rules of the Road: Using adaptations of Nagel-Schreckenberg Cellular Automaton Traffic Simulations to Evaluate Passing Rules for Multi-Lane Freeways

limitations: All 17 pages were rendered and visually reviewed.
The source's p6 randomization prose says speed is increased while the printed equation decrements speed; the record preserves the ambiguity.
The paper has no official problem statement in the corpus; task reconstruction uses author prose only.
Charts are legible but the paper does not provide raw series values, code, or seeds.

deliverables: Evaluate whether the Keep-Right-Except-to-Pass convention is safe and efficient.
Compare it against No Rules, No Lane Changes, and Middle Lane Rule variants.
Use a common multilane traffic simulator to compare flow and accident outcomes across scenarios.
Discuss the left-driving symmetry and modeling limitations before making a recommendation.
task_reconstruction.reconstruction_limit: No official statement was located; author prose is used solely to reconstruct tasks and never to classify the manifest's path-derived A label.

section_map.summary: Five-paragraph summary of four conventions, flow-safety tradeoffs, model sensitivity, and a bounded keep-right recommendation.
Practical traffic-rule context, explicit comparison question, alternative rule names, outputs, scenario axes, and work map.
Locates discrete and continuous traffic-model alternatives before choosing the CA baseline.
Defines single-lane cell occupancy and four visually checked baseline updates.
Lists closed-region, homogeneous-car, weather-proxy, reaction-time, and collision simplifications.
Constructs an n by 3 multilane state, accident process, and common CA sequence.
Completes lane, measurement, accident, and return-lane operations.
Defines repetitions, horizon, scenario levels, and flow/accident aggregation.
Paired baseline flow and accident charts.
Paired free-lane flow and accident charts.
Paired no-overtaking flow and accident charts.
Paired middle-lane flow and accident charts.
Explains chart patterns and conditional policy tradeoffs.
Begins explicit sequential-update, accident-model, and external-comparison limits.
States left-driving symmetry and parameter sensitivities.
Prioritizes safety over observed flow gains in the source simulator.
Bibliography only; excluded from positive author-language evidence.

contributions.summary: Retains the four local single-lane CA operations as a transparent inherited baseline.
Stores lane in an n by 3 matrix, permits cross-lane same-cell positions, and adds a lane-change stage.
Adds accident detection, negative-speed freeze markers, lane blocking, exit counts, cycling, and designated-lane return.
Uses ten runs of 250 steps over a stated condition grid to produce flow and accident summaries.
Connects lane freedom, blocked lanes, return behavior, and chain reactions to conditional internal rankings.
Separates left-driving representation symmetry from the strong implementation and density sensitivities.

edges: task and policy set -> assumptions -> M1 -> M3
M3/M4 -> M5 flow and accident metrics
M6 -> M7 transfer and sensitivity boundary
feedbacks: The source identifies matrix-population and accident-probability sensitivity after chart comparison, constraining later interpretation.
The left-driving relation relabels lane state but is not independently validated with new traffic data.
dependency_graph.closure_status: The paper maintains a visible policy-to-CA-to-paired-metric-to-decision route, but external calibration, reproducible randomization, collision realism, and density control remain incomplete.

assumptions.summary: A small predefined car region stands for an entire freeway despite possible spatial variation.
No car enters or exits during an individual simulation, fixing the studied density.
Cars are identical and separated by integer cell lengths.
Accident-rate probability is used to cover weather conditions without a weather mechanism.
Driver reaction times are random and determine prevention of a potential accident.
Only two-car same-lane collisions occur; simultaneous three-car and cross-lane collisions are excluded.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Each policy-condition output averages ten 250-step simulations on a 100-cell region.
Fast Vmax=6 and slow Vmax=2 cells per time step are the stated speed regimes.
Computer=0, normal=.01, and accident-prone=.3 are the stated random speed-increase conditions.
Heavy has 100 cars and light has 30 cars in the source setup.
Average flow is total exits averaged across ten simulations divided by 250; average accidents are mean raw accident counts.

models.summary: MU-A-2014-31333-001: Provide the inherited discrete traffic baseline and its four ordered local updates.
MU-A-2014-31333-002: Bound the CA's spatial, population, behavioral, weather, and collision transfer domain.
MU-A-2014-31333-003: Extend the baseline CA with lateral motion, cycling, accident counting, lane locking, and rule-specific return behavior.
MU-A-2014-31333-004: Hold the CA platform fixed while varying lateral freedom, start-lane placement, and designated-lane return behavior.
MU-A-2014-31333-005: Generate comparable finite-run flow and accident summaries across policy, lanes, speed, accident probability, and car-count scenarios.
MU-A-2014-31333-006: Translate aligned CA outputs into conditional statements about efficiency, safety, and model mechanisms.
MU-A-2014-31333-007: Separate the left-driving index transformation from empirical validation and identify lane-count and accident-probability sensitivities.

verification.summary: Ten repeated finite simulations provide internal averaging, not a seed-controlled uncertainty analysis.
Paired flow and accident outcomes establish the incumbent within-model baseline.
Paired charts test the free-lane convention on the same stated outputs.
Paired charts test the no-overtaking counterfactual.
Paired charts test middle-lane behavior only where a middle lane exists.
A cited different circular-track model is used as contextual contrast, not equivalent external validation.
The authors explicitly disclose lane-count and accident-probability sensitivity.

results_trace.summary: No Rules is reported as the highest-flow alternative but with a higher typical three-lane accident rate than keep-right.
No Lane Changes is reported as second-highest flow yet higher accident rate for typical three-lane highways.
Middle Lane Rule is reported as lowest flow and highest accident rate among the four conventions.
No Rules is stated to improve safety relative to right-hand rule only at high lane counts within the source model.
No Change's high accident count is attributed to blocked-lane accident chain reactions.
The authors choose the right-hand convention because safety is prioritized over the faster No Rules and No Change flows.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A compact paired flow-safety result route may improve reviewability, but award status does not establish a causal judge preference.
Making repetition count, horizon, scenario values, and metric aggregation explicit may support auditability, but no official scoring evidence is supplied.
Showing both efficiency and safety for each convention makes a policy tradeoff inspectable rather than proving a preference for any chart form.

weaknesses.summary: The p6 prose calls randomization a speed increase while the printed update is v -> v-1, so an implementation cannot silently choose one.
The paper says the model steps act individually in limitations, while its inherited baseline described simultaneous updates; conflict ordering is not fully reconciled.
The +/- lane equations do not fully specify target choice, simultaneous conflicts, or tie resolution.
Negative speeds -1 or -5 encode a freeze but the equation does not define exact clearing duration or its relation to response time.
Ten-run averages omit seeds, raw outcomes, warm-up, confidence intervals, and scenario-table enumeration.
The No Change discussion cites the second figure of Section 4.2.4 despite that subsection being Middle Lane Rule.
The cited circular-track no-lane-change model does not include the same accident process or policy mapping.
The MATLAB matrix cap makes density fall as lane count rises, confounding claimed lane-count effects.
Only three accident-probability values are tested despite a stated nonlinear response and chain reactions.
The conclusion prefers keep-right without external crash, traffic, enforcement, or behavior validation.

independent_extensions.summary: Specify a parallel or explicitly serial update order, lane-target conflict resolution, accident-clearance process, and seeded stochastic protocol before comparing lane policies.
Publish a full factorial scenario table, raw replicate outcomes, warm-up, seeds, confidence intervals, and normalized flow and safety measures.
Hold density, demand, and physical road length constant when varying lane count; analyze lane capacity separately from population constraints.
Calibrate car-following, lane changing, crash surrogates, weather, entry-exit behavior, and enforcement constraints against observed traffic before recommending a rule.

candidate_rule_impacts.basis: Path-classified A language evidence is source-anchored; reusable rhetorical mechanisms retain boundaries and anti-copy tests.
The paper visibly traces its policy question through a shared CA, paired outputs, limits, and conclusion.
Published repetitions and parameter values help reproducibility, while absent seeds, raw outcomes, and complete execution protocols remain explicit.
The source keeps rule choices tied to stated assumptions, paired flow and accident outputs, and an explicit safety-first objective priority.
